## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy-header test should be fixed: its input has no `END` line and keeps a `REPORT v1` header, so it never reaches the version check it is named for. The tests were read, not run.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts a report only when its first line is exactly `REPORT v1`, where it previously accepted any first line starting with `REPORT `. The pull request adds two rejection tests to `tests/test_report.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — Make the legacy-header test reach the version check — The input built here is `REPORT v1\nversion=v0` with no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at `app/report.py:3` before the version check. `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces the body's `v1`, not the header's, contradicting the line 9 comment "changing the fixture's version to v0". — This test passes whether or not the version check works, so it adds no regression protection for legacy headers. — Fix: Build the input as `REPORT v0\nversion=v1\nEND`, or delete the test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers a `v0` header.

## Suggestions
- app/report.py:5 — tests — Add a test for a header that extends `REPORT v1` — A header such as `REPORT v10` is rejected by the new equality check, but no test passes one. The only rejecting test with an `END` line uses `REPORT v0`, which a prefix check `startswith("REPORT v1")` also rejects. — A later change to a prefix match would accept `REPORT v10` reports while every existing test still passes.
